subject: c10-sst
note: Marks are official (theory total 80, four subjects at 20 each; map pointing is 5 marks in all, 2 in History and 3 in Geography). Board exam rules in the course structure: Making of a Global World only subtopics 1 to 1.3; Age of Industrialisation is assessed in periodic assessment only; Lifelines of National Economy is map pointing only; Globalisation and the Indian Economy covers the first two subtopics. Question types: MCQ 20 x 1, 2-mark answers 4 x 2, 3-mark answers 5 x 3, case studies 3 x 4, 5-mark answers 4 x 5, plus map pointing 5. Competency mix: remembering and understanding 24 marks, applying 11, analysing, evaluating and creating 40, map skill 5.
mistakes: Practise map pointing for History and Geography regularly. It is 5 marks, and marking and labelling take practice.
Case-study questions: read the source carefully and answer from it, not from memory alone.
Five-mark answers: organise the answer in clear points with an introduction, key points with examples or dates, and a short conclusion.
Learn key terms and definitions exactly, as many MCQs test them.
Do not spend board-exam time on parts that are periodic-assessment-only or project-only. Check the course structure notes above.
order: All four subjects carry 20 marks each, so give them balanced time.
Start with History and Geography, so you can practise map pointing from the beginning.
Then Political Science and Economics, which are short enough to revise more than once.
Read Age of Industrialisation (Ch 4) and the project work (Ch 22) for school assessments, not for the board paper.
